title: Unannounced and Short-Notice Exits in C&I Exit Damages
content:
**Q. Under Commercial and Industrial Electricity Contracts, what rule governs notice before the exit in contract exits?**

A. The exit damages rate is scaled by the exit notice, the calendar days from the termination notice date to the close date: a contract with no termination notice date scales it by 1.10, a notice dated fewer than the structure's termination notice days before the close date scales it by 1.05, and any longer notice leaves it unscaled. Scaling multiplies the exit damages rate per kWh by the figure shown.

| Structure | Termination notice days |
|---|---|
| Beacon Ridge C&I Real-Time Index | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Block and Index | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed Energy with Capacity and Transmission Pass-Through | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed Energy with Capacity Pass-Through | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In | 30 |
| Beacon Ridge C&I Fixed All-In Renewable | 30 |

## Questions answered

**Where is the notice found?** As the termination notice date on the contract record; a contract with none recorded is unannounced.

**How are the days counted?** In calendar days from the termination notice date to the close date, the notice date not counted.

**Where do the bands break?**

| Termination notice date | Close date | Days | Multiplier |
|---|---|---|---|
| none recorded | 17 March 2026 | none | 1.10 |
| 16 February 2026 | 17 March 2026 | 29 | 1.05 |
| 15 February 2026 | 17 March 2026 | 30 | 1, unscaled |
| 2 January 2026 | 17 March 2026 | 74 | 1, unscaled |
